Thanks for the tag. Technical proposal below — I kept it concise for contract language.

Measurement surface
- Latency measured at the public API gateway (ingress) for each request. Time is measured from request arrival to first byte returned for streaming endpoints and to final token returned for non-streaming.
- Measurements are per-region (region = cloud region where request was routed), and we report region-specific percentiles.

Percentile targets (text generation, ~256 tokens context + response):
- p50 <= 60 ms
- p95 <= 350 ms

Window and aggregation
- SLOs calculated on a 30-day rolling window (last 30 full days).
- Percentiles computed on successful requests only (2xx responses). Requests excluded: scheduled maintenance windows, documented force majeure or provider-side region outages, and customer-caused throttling or malformed requests.
- We exclude the first N warm-up tokens for newly loaded model containers; effect on tail is minimal with our continuous-batching runtime but worth noting.

Measurement notes and caveats
- Different model families and sequence-lengths materially affect latency. SLA above is scoped to the model family we plan to serve for FinWare (r-instruct-13B-1) and average request sizes described in the attached measurement_spec.xlsx. If FinWare chooses a larger model or significantly longer sequences, targets need adjustment.
- For customers in regions where we do not have HA presence (e.g., cross-region traffic to US from APAC), observed p95 can be higher due to network transport; we generally offer a negotiable exception or recommend Dedicated/Private deployment for tighter guarantees.

Exception proposal for APAC (requested):
- Temporary negotiated APAC exception: p95 <= 800 ms (30-day rolling) for up to 90 days while we onboard a regional replica. After 90 days we re-evaluate and either commit to the standard p95 <= 350 ms or provide a roadmap to Dedicated capacity with a firm date.
- Exceptions are explicitly timeboxed and listed in the SLA appendix.

Credits and remediation
- If a region misses the p95 target for a full calendar month (after excluding scheduled maintenance and documented outages) we propose a service credit equal to 10% of that month’s hosted usage for the impacted product. Caps and escalation handled in legal.

I attached a draft SLA PDF for contract redline — it contains the language above plus measurement definitions and an example calculation. Happy to join a call and walk through the specifics.

—Logan

Marissa / Logan / Vivek — thanks, this is exactly what our team needed. A few items from our side:

- We accept the p50/p95 targets (60 ms / 350 ms) for the scoped model and request they be included per-region in the SLA.
- APAC exception is acceptable but we need the exception clause to specify it expires automatically after 90 days unless both parties sign an extension.
- Credits: we request the cap on cumulative monthly credits not exceed 25% of monthly hosted fees. If possible, add an escalation step (10 business days) before credit issuance to allow mitigation.
- Please include an example p95 calculation in the SLA appendix so our procurement can validate the metric.

If you can send a revised PDF with those three bullets addressed, procurement will start the redline. We remain on track for the Nov 14 deadline.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a 30-minute call if helpful.
